newsitem.title: USA: Western Resources drops bid for ADT.
newsitem.headline: Western Resources drops bid for ADT.

text.p: Kansas utility Western Resources Inc said Wednesday it was dropping a $3.5 billion hostile bid for ADT Ltd.
The end of the seven-month effort paves the way for electronic security giant ADT to merge with Tyco International Ltd in a friendly deal valued at $5.4 billion.

Western, which owns 27 percent of ADT, said it will reap a $710 million gain on its conversion of ADT shares into Tyco stock. It said it will pursue a Bermuda court action against ADT that is related to the value of its ADT holdings.
The utility had been expected to drop the bid, which orignially was valued at $22.50 per share. Last month, it cancelled a June 17 shareholders meeting on the proposed acquisition.
ADT had disclosed in May that it was in talks with Western about dropping the bid. Western had never confirmed those discussions.

Western launched its takeover effort in December after slowly amassing a big stake in the Bermuda-based company. The bid was widely considered too low for a company that is a key player in the booming electronic security industry.
